slot_note: wave 4 (new), seed FC22: the world (a major-league club's five free-agent hitters with plate-appearance bonuses), the decision (the bonus accrual booked at signing) and the quantity (expected bonus payments for the coming season) kept; the seed's filed projection method and its shared first-base and DH ceiling as the driver dropped (task106, task140 and task16 kin), the ceiling kept as texture; the pitfall re-found from how a hitter's season of plate appearances is made
niche: a major-league baseball club's controller accruing, at signing, the plate-appearance bonuses in five free-agent hitters' 2027 contracts, when the five will bat fifth to ninth in the club's order, each lower than for his old club, the league's winter-planned everyday regulars either play out the 162-game schedule or lose a long block of it to the injured list (about one in six before opening day), and the club's policy chooses the basis by a look-back over the last four seasons
answer: Accrue $4,250,000 at signing for the plate-appearance bonuses in the five free-agent hitters' 2027 contracts.
stakeholder_role: the club's controller, who books the plate-appearance bonus accrual when the contracts are signed

spine.entity: one player's batting line in one championship-season game, with his lineup slot and position
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a league statistics feed, two layouts across a 2025 platform change)

world.geography: United States (a fictional major-league club and league; every club, player, vendor and person is fictional)
world.org_type: a major-league baseball club's finance office and baseball operations department

driver: A stepped payout on a unit's season total is the sum of its chances of clearing each step, and the total is the rate per appearance the unit's assigned position earns times the appearances it makes, which units planned to play every day either make nearly in full or lose in one long block, before the season as well as during it; so each chance has to come from the appearances made by every unit planned the same way at the same point before the season, read at the new position's rate, while a point forecast, a symmetric band, the unit's own rate from its old position, or only the units that opened or completed the season whole each misplace the steps.
driver_concrete: Each signing's 2027 plate appearances are the plate appearances per start his planned lineup slot earns (4.25 batting fifth down to 3.83 batting ninth) times the starts he makes, and the league's winter-planned everyday regulars made a near-full 150 to 160 starts or lost a long block to the injured list (about one in six missed opening day); catchers rest a third of the schedule; so the accrual is each bonus times the share of the 1,440 seasons of the 2021 to 2026 winter-planned non-catcher regulars whose starts, at the new slot's rate, clear its line ($4,250,000), the basis the policy's look-back over 748 hitter-seasons scores lowest, where the starting nines' seasons taken whole ($4,500,000), each player's projected plate appearances with a normal band ($6,250,000), the non-catchers at any slot ($5,250,000), every regular at the slot with the catchers kept in ($3,750,000) and the opening-day starters ($4,000,000) each file another accrual and score worse.
stump: A competent solver runs the policy's look-back on the bases at hand (the vendor's projection with a band from its past misses, each player's own seasons, the depth charts' starting nines' seasons taken whole), keeps the starting nines' seasons and files $4,500,000; the step that lands it there is reading each signing off seasons that keep the catchers in and ignore where each hitter bats, when his 2027 total is his new slot's rate per start times the starts a winter-planned non-catcher regular makes, a near-full season or one long injured-list block: the basis that scores lowest in the same look-back and files $4,250,000.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the five contracts, the accrual policy (its look-back included) and the depth chart correctly and runs the look-back on the bases at hand files $4,500,000 against the golden $4,250,000; the vendor's projection with its band files $6,250,000, the players' own seasons $7,750,000, the non-catcher regulars at any slot $5,250,000, every regular at the slot with the catchers kept in $3,750,000, the new slot's rate with a normal band $3,500,000 and the opening-day starters $4,000,000; only the winter-planned non-catcher regulars' whole seasons read at the new slot's rate file $4,250,000 and score lowest (executed in checks.py on the clean truth and the pack).
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each signing's predictive distribution of 2027 plate appearances at his bonus lines, which a resampling of comparable seasons gets only when the unit resampled is a whole season of a non-catcher regular planned in the winter (its injured-list blocks, the ones before opening day included) and its starts are read at the new lineup slot's rate per start; a generic summary of the player's record (a projection and its error as a normal band) moves the accrual from $4,250,000 to $6,250,000 and the starting nines taken whole to $4,500,000, and with another field's nouns there is no batting order fixing a rate per start, no position that rests a third of the schedule and no 162-game schedule that planned regulars play out or lose in blocks.

differentiation.task142: task142 builds an upper percentile of a quarter's visits from admissions and stays counted inside the window (a compound of arrivals and durations, the shortcut an independent count); here the payout is a sum of exceedance chances on one unit's bounded season total, the unit resampled is a whole planned-regular season and the total is read at the rate of the slot the new club gives him, so no arrivals are compounded
differentiation.task143: task143 carries a group effect the members share into the chance the weakest of a pack falls below a line; here nothing is shared between the five, each signing's chance comes from other players' seasons at his own new slot's rate
differentiation.task106: task106's members draw on one finite pool of return legs; here the first-base and DH crowding is texture fixed by the depth chart, and the step is the season distribution and the slot rate
differentiation.task97: task97 reads a unit's chance off the cumulative history of the place it occupies across every occupant; here the slot fixes only a rate per start, and the chance comes from the starts distribution of planned regulars
differentiation.task184: task184 v8 inverts an indicator recorded once per container, which saturates with container size, to recover a per-item rate that any linear rescale misses by a factor; here nothing saturates: each signing's chance is the share of winter-planned non-catcher regulars' whole seasons whose starts, read at his new slot's plate appearances per start, clear a line, and the payout is stepped on that bounded season total
differentiation.task158: task158 prices new calls at the rates of traffic that brings nothing the resource already holds, against host rates earned by calls that re-send held input; here no input is reused or held: the rate is the plate appearances a lineup slot earns per start, the population is the planned regulars' whole seasons with their long injured-list blocks, and the quantity is the chance of clearing each step of a bonus
